review_notes: I read the whole file. I also read the sibling lemmas it uses: mem_zigzagProjectiveGrade_iff, zigzagGradedProjective_piece, mem_zigzagProjectiveRadicalPower_iff and GradedModuleCat.mem_ofIdeal_piece_iff. The existing @[simp] lemmas (coe_zigzagGradedSocleVolume, zigzagGradedHeadToSocle_mk, zigzagGradedHeadIsoSocle_hom_apply, zigzagGradedHeadIsoSocle_inv_volume) look sound. Their LHS are in normal form and they are not obviously competing or cyclic. I found no loop or competing-rule problem. The one finding is a gap in the simp interface and is modest. I did not run Lean, so I cannot say whether the proposed simp attribute would work in the affected proofs.

findings.excerpt:
theorem mem_zigzagGradedProjectiveSocle_piece_iff (i : V) (p : ℤ)
    (x : zigzagGradedProjectiveSocle k G hns i) :
    x ∈ (zigzagGradedProjectiveSocle k G hns i).grading.piece p ↔
      (x : Z) ∈ zigzagIntegerGrade k G p := by
findings.problem: This is the canonical membership characterization for the graded socle's pieces. It is not tagged @[simp]. The analogous lemma for the projective, `mem_zigzagProjectiveGrade_iff`, is @[simp] (Basic.lean line 120) and has the same shape: membership in a graded piece iff the coerced algebra element lies in `zigzagIntegerGrade`. The graded-socle version is the odd one out. As a result, goals of the form `x ∈ (zigzagGradedProjectiveSocle ..).grading.piece p` are not reduced to the ambient algebra by `simp`. The file uses it only through manual `rw` or `.1`, for example in `zigzagGradedSocleVolume_mem_grade_two` and `positiveIdeal_smul_socleVolume`. Those proofs must pass the explicit arguments `k G hns i 2 _` and sequence `rw`s together with `▸`. Because `coe_zigzagGradedSocleVolume` is @[simp], tagging the membership lemma would let `simp` take a piece-membership goal for the volume all the way down to `zigzagVolume k G i ∈ zigzagIntegerGrade k G 2`.
findings.proposed_change: Add `@[simp]` to `mem_zigzagGradedProjectiveSocle_piece_iff`. The rewrite direction is safe: the RHS is a plain ambient-algebra membership with strictly simpler structure. Then `zigzagGradedSocleVolume_mem_grade_two` can be reduced to `simp` plus the existing `zigzagProjectiveVolume_mem_grade_two`, instead of the `rw` / `▸` / `rwa` chain.
findings.benefit: The socle API then matches the projective API, where `mem_zigzagProjectiveGrade_iff` is @[simp]. Downstream proofs about graded-socle piece membership shrink to `simp`, and users need not know the lemma name or its explicit argument order.
